prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stocks with a Case to Beat the S&P 500 Over the Next Year

No one can reliably predict which stocks will beat the index over 12 months. In most years, most professional large-cap fund managers underperform the S&P 500, and over 15 years about 9 in 10 do. A 10-stock portfolio can beat the index by a wide margin or trail it by a wide margin. Also, my information only runs through about May 2026, so check current prices and news before acting on any of this.

## The 10 stocks

| # | Stock | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes nearly all advanced AI chips for Nvidia, Apple, AMD and Broadcom. It isn't in the S&P 500, so it adds something the index lacks. | China–Taiwan tensions |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Leading designer of custom AI chips for Google, Meta and others, plus steady VMware software revenue | High valuation; a few customers make up much of its revenue |
| 3 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Search is still very profitable, Google Cloud is growing fast, and it owns Gemini, its own AI chips and Waymo. It has usually traded cheaper than other megacaps. | Antitrust rulings; AI chatbots taking search traffic |
| 4 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS is benefiting from AI demand, retail profit margins are rising, and advertising is a large, high-margin business | Heavy spending on data centers weighing on free cash flow |
| 5 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines and grid equipment for data centers and electrification, with a multi-year order backlog | Stock has already risen a lot, so high expectations are priced in |
| 6 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leader in obesity drugs (Zepbound), with a pill version (orforglipron) coming | Drug price pressure, competition, premium valuation |
| 7 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-run large US bank, with a possible boost from lighter regulation and more deal-making | A weakening economy causing more loan losses |
| 8 | **MercadoLibre (MELI)** | Leading e-commerce and payments company in Latin America, growing much faster than US peers. Also not in the S&P 500. | Latin American currencies and politics |
| 9 | **UnitedHealth (UNH)** | Contrarian pick: the stock collapsed on rising medical costs, a DOJ investigation and weak Medicare Advantage payment rates, so a recovery could bring a big rebound | The problems could last longer than expected |
| 10 | **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)** | Stabilizer: a large cash pile and diversified businesses that help if markets fall. It is now led by Greg Abel. | Likely to lag in a strong bull market |

## How to use this list

- **To beat the index, you have to own something different from it.** Alphabet, Amazon and Broadcom are already among the S&P 500's biggest holdings. Most of any outperformance would come from TSM, MELI, GEV, LLY and UNH.
- **Watch your AI exposure.** Five of the ten (TSM, AVGO, GOOGL, AMZN, GEV) depend partly on AI spending continuing. If that spending slows, they could fall together.
- **Consider a core-and-satellite setup.** For example, put 70–80% in a low-cost S&P 500 fund (VOO, SPY, or CSPX for non-US investors) and 20–30% in these picks. You still have a real shot at beating the index without risking a large shortfall.
- **Keep position sizes equal.** About 10% each prevents one bad pick from sinking the portfolio.
- **Write down each reason for buying.** In 12 months, compare your results with the index and check whether those reasons held up, not just whether the price went up.

This isn't personalized advice, since I don't know your finances, time horizon or tax situation. If you tell me your risk tolerance, how much you plan to invest, and which country you invest from, I can adjust the list.
